Matched perturbation: Change association while constraining bulk transport and the surface
Observation favouring or limiting the ex: Population-resolved Raman/NMR plus transport controls: a reactive-carrier increase tracks Mg current at unchanged exchange; conductivity or film changes leave the assignment unresolved

Matched perturbation: Change donor/anion identity on compatibly conditioned surfaces
Observation favouring or limiting the ex: Resolved-ligand exchange NMR or validated MD plus Mg-specific current: matched exchange and rate responses support rearrangement; unchanged Mg current locates a later limitation

Matched perturbation: Follow Mg-specific current, gas and soluble/film products
Observation favouring or limiting the ex: Gas analysis and soluble/film-product balance: reduced H₂ or decomposition at unchanged exchange favours selectivity; a shell assignment alone does not establish it

Matched perturbation: Track active anion and products with increasing Mg throughput
Observation favouring or limiting the ex: Calibrated anion assay and products versus Mg throughput: active-species recovery with a repeated kinetic effect supports reuse; survival alone is compatible with a spectator

Matched perturbation: Measure residence and escape from the occupied state
Observation favouring or limiting the ex: Residence analysis and sampled free-energy path: a persistent state with a large barrier from its local minimum supports trapping; a low cluster energy alone does not

Matched perturbation: Change liquid while verifying persistence of the treated surface
Observation favouring or limiting the ex: Paired liquid replacement with surface/impedance checks: a benefit following an intact film favours surface retention; film dissolution makes a lost benefit ambiguous

Matched perturbation: Separate the initial liquid response from the retained-surface response
Observation favouring or limiting the ex: Initial response, product balance and retained-surface test: separate changes requiring both liquid and film favour coupling; CE alone cannot apportion them
